newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa carries 1.7 pct more passengers in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa carries 1.7 pct more passengers in 1996.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Monday its group activities carried a total 41.4 million passengers in 1996, a rise of 1.7 percent on the year before.
Its overall load factor, or usage of capacity, slipped by 0.2 percentage points to 70.2 percent for the year. Its passenger load factor also fell 0.2 points to 70.3 percent.

Lufthansa said in a statement its Lufthansa CityLine unit, which operates smaller aircraft between European cities, saw the largest increase. It carried 3.1 million passengers, up 17.4 percent on the year before.

Its Condor holiday flight operator received 6.6 million flight bookings, 7.3 percent up on the year before. The Lufthansa parent company however saw its passenger headcount drop 0.6 percent to 31.8 million.
Total freight and post carried increased 3.3 percent to 1.67 million tonnes, while the total number of flights rose 2.6 percent to 595,120.

Available capacity, measured in tonnes-kilometres, rose 3.6 percent to 20.7 million, while capacity sold rose at a slightly slower rate of 3.3 percent to 14.5 million, thus accounting for the small drop in the load factor.
Lufthansa said preliminary business figures for the 1996 year were expected to be known around the end of March.
